title: Dedicated fleet residency, routing and scalability controls
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement controls and policies for multi-zone and regional Dedicated fleets to provide predictable throughput guarantees, configurable autoscaling behavior, and enforceable data residency constraints. This ticket covers routing rules, placement preferences, controlled failover behavior, and control-plane changes required to express and honor residency contracts.
background: Customers running Dedicated pools require firm throughput SLAs and explicit data residency. Current routing and fleet-placement behavior is zone-first with best-effort failover; we lack a first-class policy surface for residency constraints, quota-backed throughput guarantees, and deterministic autoscaling policies that respect residency and capacity isolation.
goals: Define and implement a placement policy API for region-level and multi-zone Dedicated fleets that supports preferred zones, strict residency, and soft-failover semantics
Add throughput reservation primitives (per-fleet throughput units) that are consumed by runtime and surfaced in billing/console
Provide autoscaling policies that are aware of throughput reservations and residency constraints and can be restricted to region-local capacity
Create safe failover strategies that minimize cross-region data movement and preserve residency contracts while maximizing availability
scope_includes: Control plane API additions for placement policy and throughput reservation
Scheduler/routing changes to enforce residency on allocation and failover
Autoscaler policy primitives: target-utilization, min/max nodes, burst windows, region-only scaling flag
Console UI fields to display residency and throughput guarantees
Telemetry and dashboards to track reservation utilization, cross-zone failovers, and SLA attainment
scope_excludes: On-prem agent installation flows (handled in private deployment backlog)
Billing engine integration beyond tagging usage (separate billing ticket)
proposed_design_summary: Introduce FleetPolicy v1 with fields: residency_mode (strict|preferred|none), allowed_regions, allowed_zones, failover_policy (immediate|graceful|disabled), throughput_units (integer), scale_policy (target_utilization, min_nodes, max_nodes, region_only boolean). The control plane validates constraints at fleet creation and exposes admission checks. The scheduler reserves throughput_units on allocation and denies requests that would exceed guaranteed capacity unless override is requested. Failover follows a priority list: same-zone preferred, region-local second, cross-region only if strict residency is not required. Autoscaler respects region_only and will attempt scale-up in allowed regions first, with configurable burst windows for short-term spikes.
tradeoffs: Strict residency increases risk of unserved traffic during regional outages; we mitigate with conservative reservable spare capacity sizing and optional soft-failover
Throughput reservations improve predictability but reduce aggregate statistical multiplexing efficiency, raising unit cost; recommend reservation tier pricing
Implementing region-aware autoscaling increases scheduler complexity and might lengthen scale decisions; we will instrument decisions and iterate on heuristics
rollout_plan: Feature flag FleetPolicy v1 behind dedicated-capacity feature gate
Phase 1 (canary): enable for small set of enterprise customers with non-critical workloads and collect telemetry
Phase 2 (pilot): open to sales-managed customers with SLA contracts and run guided onboarding
Phase 3 (general): default enabled for new Dedicated fleets; migration tooling for existing fleets to opt-in
Post-launch: iterate on autoscaler heuristics based on observed failover and utilization metrics
acceptance_criteria: Control plane exposes FleetPolicy with described fields and validation tests
Scheduler enforces residency on new allocations and honors allowed_regions/allowed_zones
Throughput reservation primitive prevents allocations that would exceed guaranteed units; integration tests demonstrate enforcement under contention
Autoscaler respects region_only flag and uses target_utilization to drive scale decisions; e2e tests simulate spike and verify region-local scale-up
Console surfaces residency status and reservation utilization and an audit log for failovers
Runbook updated with failover playbook and rollback steps
test_plan: Unit tests for FleetPolicy validation and admission controller
Scheduler integration tests: create conflicting placement requests and assert correct denials and routing
Chaos experiments: simulate zone outage and validate soft-failover behavior and residency honors
Load tests: verify throughput reservation prevents oversubscription under high QPS
Canary deployment with synthetic traffic and SLA monitoring dashboards
migration_plan: Provide CLI/console migration helper that computes recommended throughput_units based on 7-day historical usage
Allow staged cutover: create new Fleet with FleetPolicy and migrate traffic using weighted routing over 48h
Fallback: revert routing weights to previous fleet and mark policy as failed if regressions observed
risks_mitigations: Risk: Over-reservation leads to wasted capacity. Mitigation: offer tooling to recommend reservation levels and burst windows to increase multiplexing efficiency
Risk: Strict residency causes unavailability during regional outage. Mitigation: conservative spare capacity and optional graceful failover with audit consent
Risk: Scheduler performance regressions. Mitigation: benchmark changes and keep legacy fast-path for non-policy fleets for 8 weeks of telemetry
